subject: Commercial pathing for VPC — amortization, credits, and SLA carveouts
messages:
From: Sandra Li <sandra.li@medirev.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medirev.com
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:16:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial questions on private VPC licensing and platform fee

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the detailed demo last week. We have two parallel streams in procurement and finance trying to model how Redwood's private VPC packaging would show up in our budget and audit trail. A few concrete items they asked me to confirm before we go to legal/SOW: 

- How do you typically invoice the platform fee for private/VPC deployments? Upfront single payment, annual invoice, or amortized monthly? Our finance team prefers amortization to match their budget window.
- Is there flexibility to treat the platform fee as a capitalized cost with an invoice schedule that supports our FY27 recognition?
- Are migration credits or implementation credits available for customers moving from a managed hosted setup to private VPC?
- For regulated workloads (PHI), what support tier do you recommend? Is an on-call SME included or charged separately?

Can you send a short term sheet and an example payment schedule we can give to our procurement team? We are targeting a decision by mid-July.

Appreciate it —
Sandra Li
Head of Procurement
MediRev Health

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sandra Li <sandra.li@medirev.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, procurement@medirev.com
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial questions on private VPC licensing and platform fee

Sandra —

Great questions. I've pulled together the short answers below and attached a preliminary term sheet for visibility. Happy to hop on a quick call with procurement/finance if that helps.

High-level options (private VPC):
1) Upfront platform fee + annual support: standard for short commitments; platform fee billed up front, support invoiced annually.
2) Amortized platform fee (our common request): we invoice the platform fee either monthly or quarterly over a defined period (typically 36 months) — this is an invoicing cadence we can support. For accounting treatment, customers can choose to capitalize depending on their internal policy; we provide the invoice schedule and payment receipts.
3) Committed-capacity discount: with a committed GPU / capacity baseline (12–24 months), we can offer reduced platform fee and lower unit pricing.

Migration / implementation credits: we typically offer a one-time migration credit equivalent to 1 month of the platform fee for customers who sign a commitment by a target date. For larger commitments we can increase the credit.

Support tier guidance: for PHI workloads we recommend Premium Support (24/7 P1 + named on-call SME and quarterly runbooks). Premium can be included as part of a committed bundle or purchased a la carte.

Next steps: I've attached a draft term sheet (Redwood_VPC_TermSheet_MediRev_20260628.pdf) and a sample SOW (SOW-Dedicated-Edge-20260628.docx). If you want, I can schedule a 30-minute calibration call with Lauren (commercial ops) to run through payment schedules and the DocuSign path.

I'll keep the target of mid-July in mind for an internal concession if you can commit to a 12–24 month minimum.

— Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Commercial questions on private VPC licensing and platform fee

Sandra / team —

Looping in more detail on the commercial mechanics so procurement has a concrete schedule they can review. Below are two pragmatic structures we use; both include SOC2 and standard security deliverables for PHI customers.

A) Standard (36-month amortization) — Recommended for predictable OPEX
- Platform fee (one-time): $360,000 — amortizable over 36 months at $10,000/mo if you select monthly invoicing.
- Dedicated capacity (GPU hours): metered monthly based on committed baseline; overage billed monthly.
- Support (Premium): $15,000/month (includes named SME, 24/7 P1) — can be prepaid annually or invoiced monthly.
- Migration credit: one-time credit equal to $10,000 (1 month platform fee) if SOW signed by July 20.
- Invoice schedule: month 1 invoice includes first amortized platform fee installment + first month support + initial capacity estimate.

B) Capital-friendly (upfront invoice, extended amortization for internal finance) — For customers needing capital treatment
- Platform fee invoiced upfront but Redwood can provide a monthly invoice schedule and payment receipts to support capital recognition. Alternatively, we can issue a 48-month split invoice (two invoices per year) to mirror your internal recognition windows — this requires a minimum 24-month committed capacity.

Controls, SLA and carveouts:
- SLA: 99.9% service availability for production endpoints (per SOW).
- Extended SLA / penalty carveouts for multi-region failover available on a case-by-case basis.

Procurement asks we typically need: PO referencing the deal id (RDW-8342-MR), signed SOW, and a purchase order number for invoicing.

I've attached a redlineable term sheet and sample SOW. If procurement wants an amortization schedule in a specific format (e.g., quarterly for FY recognition), we can produce that formally.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Thanks Lauren — helpful detail. A couple follow-ups from Finance/CTO: 

- Platform fee: we appreciate the 36-month amortization option but would prefer an extended amortization (48 months) to match our capital plans. Is Redwood willing to stretch amortization to 48 months if we commit to a 24-month minimum GPU baseline?
- Discounting: given our expected committed GPU spend (projected 24-month consumption ~ $1.2M), can you provide an incremental discount on the platform fee (we were hoping for ~15% off list) or a larger migration credit?
- Support: we need an on-call SME guaranteed for Q1 2027 for the rollout — can that be included for the first 3 months at no additional cost?

We are aiming to finalize procurement terms and issue a PO by July 16. Appreciate any movement on amortization and the support ask — I know those are common sticking points.

Thanks for the clear ask. We want to make this an easy procurement path for MediRev while protecting our capacity economics. Concession we can offer if MediRev signs a 24-month committed capacity SOW by July 20 (deal id RDW-8342-MR):

- Amortization: extend to 42 months (we can provide an invoice schedule that maps monthly installments across 42 months). We cannot commit to 48 months without a larger committed spend, but 42 months is a middle ground we can support operationally.
- Platform fee discount: 12% off the listed platform fee as part of the 24-month commitment.
- Migration & support credit: one-time migration credit equal to $15,000 and complimentary Premium support for the first 3 months (includes named on-call SME for rollout).
- Documentation: updated term sheet and DocuSign link attached. We'll also produce a formal amortization schedule in the format MediRev prefers (monthly or quarterly) once procurement confirms PO cadence.

Conditionality: these concessions require (1) signed SOW and (2) purchase order referencing RDW-8342-MR by July 20. If you need a slightly different schedule for invoice recognition, tell us the exact dates and finance contacts and we'll try to accommodate.
